title: Care Policy Library — Cancellation and Deposit Refund Rules for Pre-Orders & Back-Orders
content:
### Clauses in force

**C1. Cancelling at will.** A customer may cancel a Pre-Orders & Back-Orders reservation at will until the type's cancellation cutoff. For every type except the Made-to-Order Reservation the cutoff is allocation. For the Made-to-Order Reservation it is the start of production.

**C2. After a delay notice.** Once any delay notice has been sent for a reservation, so that its delay-notice count is above 0, a customer cancellation is always refunded in full, whatever the status and the cutoff.

**C3. Cancellations caused by the company.** Every cancellation caused by Marlowe & Finch or its supplier refunds the deposit in full. These are cancellations for supplier cancelled, launch shortfall, delay not consented, delay cap reached and production failure.

**C4. Other full refunds.** A customer whose specifications were not confirmed in time (specifications not confirmed) receives the deposit back in full. So does a customer whose card stayed declined past the grace period (payment declined).

**C5. Where and when.** Refunds go to the original card within the type's refund period in business days. Types without a deposit took no money, so for them the card authorization is simply released.

**C6. Allocated reservations.** An allocated reservation cannot be cancelled at will. The customer may refuse delivery, or return the item under Returns & Exchanges once it is delivered.

**C7. Supplier cancellation.** Only types that the supplier can cancel may be cancelled for the reason supplier cancelled. A Deposit Pre-Order or a Made-to-Order Reservation is never cancelled that way.

### Clauses no longer in force

The following former clauses are **no longer in force**. Each has been superseded by the current basis for that subject:

- R1. The former clause that the deposit is refunded in full on a cancellation before the cutoff.
- R2. The former clause that a Made-to-Order Reservation cancelled at the customer's request after the cutoff forfeits its deposit, cancelled only on a confirmed cancellation-with-forfeiture request for that reservation.
- R3. The former clause that a refund or forfeiture is booked only once the reservation is in status cancelled.

### Full-refund grounds at a glance

| Cancellation reason | Deposit refunded in full | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| Supplier cancelled | Yes | C3 |
| Launch shortfall | Yes | C3 |
| Delay not consented | Yes | C3 |
| Delay cap reached | Yes | C3 |
| Production failure | Yes | C3 |
| Specifications not confirmed | Yes | C4 |
| Payment declined | Yes | C4 |
| Customer request, after any delay notice | Yes | C2 |

### Points of judgement

- A reservation is allocated and the customer no longer wants the item. Cancelling at will is not available (C6). The customer may refuse delivery, or return the item under Returns & Exchanges after delivery.
- A Seasonal Pre-Order, which has no deposit, is cancelled. No money was taken, so nothing is refunded to the card. Any card authorization is released (C5).
- A customer cancels a reservation that had received a delay notice. The refund is in full whatever the status (C2).

superseded_clauses: Before the cutoff the deposit is refunded in full (`deposit_refundable_before_cutoff`).

After the cutoff a Made-to-Order Reservation can still be cancelled at the customer's request, but its deposit is forfeited (`deposit_forfeited_after_cutoff`); such a cancellation is made only on a cancellation_with_forfeiture request for that reservation whose request_status is confirmed.
A refund or forfeiture is booked only once the reservation is in status cancelled.
